title: Yearbook and Semester
premise: Paloma Marchetti, a cautious transfer student at Hollowmere Academy, joins a class group chat that begins posting predictions of events before they occur—predictions tied to a 1974 fire the school board buried along with four missing students. As Paloma investigates with three unlikely allies, he discovers the chat is fed by a ledger hidden in the school's sealed sub-basement, an inheritance passed student-to-student that grants foresight at the cost of feeding on its keepers. The board's chairwoman has been harvesting the ledger for decades to protect her reputation and power, and she will silence anyone who reads it. In the climax, Paloma must choose between using the ledger's power to guarantee his own survival or destroying it to free the school from its corruption; he burns it, exposing the truth at graduation, and finally stops being careful.
about_author: Astrid Ashgrove grew up in a mill town where the high school was older than the town charter, a fact no one liked to discuss. She writes stories about teenagers who inherit other people's secrets and have to decide what they're worth.

chapters.title: The New Kid Counts Exits
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On his first day at Hollowmere Academy, Paloma maps every exit, memorizes every social hierarchy, and perfects his invisibility—a habit from twenty years of foster placements. He notices the school's odd architecture: bricked archways, a staircase to nowhere. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence, and the first flicker of unease about what the building is hiding.

chapters.title: Group Chat: Unknown Number
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A group chat called 'Semester' adds him without permission. Its first message predicts a pipe burst in the east wing—hours before it happens. Classmates dismiss it as a prank; Paloma, who notices everything, doesn't. He meets Wren, the cynical yearbook editor who created the chat as a joke, and Theo, a scholarship kid who's been receiving predictions privately for weeks. Emotional beat: wary curiosity cracking open isolation.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Doesn't Show
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Editing the 1974 yearbook digitization project, Wren finds four senior photos with names scratched out and a page torn from the binding. The fire that closed the old wing that spring killed 'no one,' according to records—but the yearbook disagrees. She brings Paloma and Theo into the archive after hours. Emotional beat: the thrill of shared purpose replacing Wren's performative detachment.

chapters.title: Predictions Get Personal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The chat starts predicting small things: a pop quiz, a fight in the quad, then Theo's brother's car accident—which they narrowly prevent by acting on the warning. Paloma realizes acting on predictions changes outcomes, but each intervention makes the messages more insistent, more intimate, quoting things only he knows. Emotional beat: terror braided with the intoxicating sense of mattering.

chapters.title: The Chairwoman's Smile
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Board chairwoman Odile Vantrease summons Theo—the scholarship student she personally sponsors—and gently warns him about 'rumors.' Theo realizes his private predictions began the week he signed her mentorship paperwork. He discovers his signature appears on documents dated decades before his birth. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into defiance as Theo understands he was chosen, not helped.

chapters.title: Below the Staircase to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following architectural anomalies, the trio finds a service door behind the auditorium and descends into the sealed sub-basement: the burned old wing, preserved like a museum. They find the ledger—a student notebook, continuously written since 1974, recording predictions in dozens of hands. The last entry is in Paloma's handwriting. He hasn't written it yet. Emotional beat: awe collapsing into dread.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Research reveals the ledger's rule: it passes keeper-to-keeper, granting true sight while slowly consuming the keeper's memory of everyone they love. The four students from 1974 weren't fire victims—they were keepers who refused to pass it on. Vantrease was their classmate who survived by feeding it victims ever since. Emotional beat: grief for the erased, and Wren's guilt over having built the chat that lured Paloma in.

chapters.title: The Price of Being Seen
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Vantrease corners Paloma, offering him everything he's ever wanted—permanence, belonging, a family—if he accepts the ledger willingly. Meanwhile his friends' faces begin slipping from his memory, the ledger collecting its advance payment. He realizes staying invisible kept him safe, but visibility is the only way anything changes. Emotional beat: the seduction of power against the horror of forgetting.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren's alternating POV. The trio executes a plan: livestream the sub-basement during the graduation ceremony while Paloma confronts Vantrease among the archived records. She traps them below as the school seals itself—doors locking exactly as predicted in the ledger's final pages. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve; the friends choose each other over safety.

chapters.title: Yearbook and Semester
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the burning-cold archive, Paloma refuses the inheritance and feeds the ledger its own final prediction, igniting it—freeing the four 1974 keepers' names back into the record. Above, the livestream exposes Vantrease; the board falls. At graduation, Paloma signs the yearbook with his full name, unable to remember his mother's face but surrounded by people who know him now. Emotional beat: costly, hard-won belonging.
